affected_boundaries: Git worktree inventory to rolling participant configuration

observed_behavior: A coordinator could not adopt rolling campaigns while historical Git worktrees lacked rolling configuration or retained absent checkout registrations.
expected_behavior: Validate the coordinator and every actual rolling participant without editing or enrolling unrelated historical checkouts.
causal_mechanism: Pool resolution treated every Git inventory entry as a configured rolling participant and eagerly resolved absent historical roots.

anti_pattern.structural_description: An inventory containing historical and current checkouts was treated as the membership authority for one configured campaign capability.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: Historical branches and retained unowned registrations do not necessarily carry the newer configuration or have an existing root.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: The coordinator, all registered roots directly in the managed pool, and all checkouts declaring rolling configuration must agree on physical pool identity.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Keep Git registration paths intact and validate configuration only for these participants; do not resolve or mutate unrelated historical checkout roots.

applicability_conditions: A repository adopts rolling campaigns after creating historical worktrees.
known_non_matches: A registered pool member missing configuration still fails.
A checkout declaring a different managed pool still fails.
confirmation_evidence: The new real-Git adoption regression failed at the missing historical primary configuration before the repair and passed after it.
regression_proofs: tests/rolling-worktrees.integration.test.ts: rolling adoption leaves unconfigured historical worktrees untouched and validates every participant
